data.narrative:
Seneca is a Series A–stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Stuart Landesberg and Nick Foley. The company has raised $60M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises eight private companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air; no direct public comparables exist in this space.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method. Using total capital raised ($60M) as a baseline value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $120M. This method reflects market norms for capital deployment and dilution across stages within the frontier-tech sector.

Peer-median triangulation was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum data thresholds (fewer than three datapoints in relevant filtering buckets). The broader peer set exists but lacks sufficient granularity to support a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. Key uncertainties center on the depth of comparable transaction data in early-stage autonomous systems and the trajectory-specific capital intensity of Seneca's technology. Additional clarity on unit economics and near-term funding requirements would refine this estimate.
